case_title: Pargan Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Stranger (the assailants were unknown to the complainant and other persons)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307, s.397, each read with s.34
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-2 injured eyewitness, PW-3 complainant); medical evidence (postmortem and injury reports); extra-judicial confession (PW-1)
confession: Extra-judicial confession made to PW-1 (Pradhan of the mohalla). Accepted by the courts below and not disturbed by the Supreme Court, but treated as a weak type of evidence needing corroboration; the Court relied mainly on the two eyewitnesses.
aggravating_circumstances: Shooting of the victim's companion who was killed; firing at a bystander who tried to stop the robbery, causing serious injury; robbery of cash during the attack
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302, 307 and 397 IPC r/w s.34; life imprisonment and Rs.50,000 fine under s.302; 10 years RI and Rs.25,000 fine under s.307; 10 years RI under s.397; sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld (judgment dated 13.12.2012)
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.34); attempt to murder (IPC s.307 r/w s.34); robbery-related offence under IPC s.397
neutral_facts: On 25 March 1999, the victim and a companion withdrew four lakh rupees in cash from a bank and rode two-wheelers back toward their office. Near a market, a black scooter carrying two men approached from behind. The pillion rider fired a pistol at the victim, who fell from the scooter. The two men snatched the money bag, which also contained a cheque book, and turned back. When the companion tried to stop them, the pillion rider fired at him, injuring him. The assailants then fled on the scooter with the money bag. The victim died from a gunshot wound to the back, with severe haemorrhage and injury to vital organs. The companion received multiple gunshot wounds to the shoulder, neck, face and tongue and lost consciousness. The complainant, who was present, reported the incident promptly to the police, and officers visited the spot and recorded the death and injuries. The assailants were unknown to the complainant and the companion. Police could not trace the culprits for several years. In July 2006 a special team was formed, and police received information identifying the accused. A local resident, described as the Pradhan of his mohalla, stated that the accused had confessed to him. The accused were arrested at a naka in August 2006 when they were seen riding a scooter. The accused declined a test identification parade. The eyewitnesses later identified the accused at trial.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a gunshot wound to the upper back with severe haemorrhage and injury to vital organs; the companion suffered multiple gunshot wounds to the shoulder, neck, face and tongue, with serious injury
financial_property_loss: Rs.4 lakhs in cash withdrawn from the bank (money bag snatched), plus a cheque book
motive: alleged: robbery of the cash bag (Rs.4 lakhs) withdrawn from the bank
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-2 (injured eyewitness) and PW-3 (complainant); extra-judicial confession to PW-1, corroborated by the two eyewitnesses; medical evidence of ante-mortem gunshot injuries
witness_credibility: The Court found PW-2 and PW-3 credible: their accounts were consistent and PW-2, as an injured witness, had a higher degree of credibility; PW-1 was a respectable Pradhan with no axe to grind
post_offence_conduct: Accused declined a test identification parade without any stated reason; no other post-offence conduct such as absconding is noted by the Court
custody_duration: Not stated (arrested 07.08.2006; duration of custody not stated)
trial_duration: offence: 25.03.1999; trial judgment: 25.09.2008; High Court: 13.12.2012; Supreme Court: 05.09.2014
legal_representation: Accused: Shreepal Singh (for Pargan Singh) and Shiv Kumar Suri (for Harminder Singh), with others listed as counsel for the appellants; State: V. Madhukar, AAG, with Anvita Cowshish and Kuldip Singh for the respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered on the complainant's statement; site inquest and seizures made; culprits not traced for years; accused arrested in August 2006; challan filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions Judge, Kapurthala): convicted; High Court: appeal dismissed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld
prosecution_argument: The eyewitnesses PW-1 and PW-2 are credible; PW-2 is an injured eyewitness; 90 seconds was enough to observe and remember the assailants; PW-1 is an independent witness; the claim that faces were shown at the police station was never pleaded earlier
defence_argument: The prosecution story is suspect; PW-2 was shown the accused at the police station before the test identification parade, so the parade had no purpose; the witnesses were unknown and the incident lasted only about 90 seconds, so identification after 7 years is unreliable; the accused were falsely implicated
legal_principle_applied: Eyewitness identification after a long gap depends on the circumstances of observation (duration and trauma); an injured witness's testimony needs higher credibility; extra-judicial confession is weak and needs corroboration; conviction may rest on credible eyewitnesses alone
precedent_relied_upon: Balwinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) Supp (4) SCC 259 (on extra-judicial confession)
